prompt: A banking ledger must be able to show exactly how every account balance was reached, and rebuild balances as of any past date.
tells: how every account balance was reached
rebuild balances as of any past date
why: Event sourcing: store every transaction as an immutable event and derive balances by replaying them.
trap: Backups and replicas capture snapshots, not the full history of how you got there.

prompt: Orders are written in a normalized model, but the mobile app, the warehouse screen and the finance report each need very different read shapes.
why: Separate the write model from purpose-built read models, kept up to date from write events.
trap: Replicas copy the same schema; they don't reshape it for each reader.

prompt: Product wants a new analytics view computed over two years of past user actions that were never stored in that form.
tells: two years of past user actions
why: If actions are kept as an event log, you can replay it to build any new projection.
trap: A queue delivers events once; an event store keeps them to replay later.

prompt: A trading system's writes need strict validation and ordering, while its dashboards need fast denormalized reads that can lag by a second.
tells: writes need strict validation and ordering
fast denormalized reads that can lag
why: Split commands and queries: a strict write side, plus read models updated asynchronously.
trap: Replicas lag too, but they keep the write-optimized schema instead of a read-optimized one.

prompt: A document editor must show a full history of changes and let users rewind to any point.
why: Event sourcing stores each change; any past state is a replay.
trap: Snapshots in object storage give points, not every step.

prompt: Orders are written to a relational database, and a separate search index and a reporting store are both updated from the stream of order events.
tells: both updated from the stream of order events
why: Separate write model and read models fed by events: CQRS.
trap: Each read store is a pattern itself, but the overall shape is CQRS.

prompt: A bug miscalculated loyalty balances for a month. Because every purchase event is stored, the team fixes the code and recomputes all balances.
why: Event sourcing lets you fix logic and replay to rebuild state.
trap: Without the event log, you'd only have the wrong balances.

prompt: Inventory writes need strict checks to avoid overselling, while the storefront needs fast stock counts per product in many views.
tells: fast stock counts per product in many views
why: Split commands (validated writes) from queries (denormalized read views).
trap: A cache helps reads, but separating models is the design.
